|\n151\t|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n152\t| `working_dir` | string | yes | **Primary project path** - absolute path to project directory |\n153\t| `description` | string | no | of different types that AgentScribe expands into canonical events:\n183\t\n184\t#### Type 1: Text Block\n185\t\n186\t```json\n187\t{\n188\t  \"type\": \"text\",\n189\t  \"text\": \"I have started a Plugin Configuration Schema\n\n### 1.1 Complete Plugin TOML\n\n```toml\n[plugin]\nname = \"goose\"\nversion = \"1.0\"\n\n[source]\npaths = [\"~/.local/share/goose/sessions/*.jsonl\"]\nexclude = []\nformat = \"jsonl\"\n\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\nsession_id_from = \"filename\"\n\n[parser]\ntimestamp = \"created\"        # Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)\nrole = \"role\"               # \"user\" or \"assistant\"\ncontent = \"content\"         # Array of content blocks\n\n[parser.static]\nsource_agent = \"goose\"\n\n[parser.project]\nmethod = \"field\"            # Extract from first-line metadata\nfield = \"working_dir\"       # Field name in session metadata (line 1)\n\n[parser.model]\nsource = \"none\"             # Model information not available in goose logs\n\n[parser.file_paths]\ncontent_regex = true        # Extract file paths from content via regex\n```\n\n### 1.2 Plugin Metadata Fields\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `name` | string | yes | Plugin identifier: \"goose\" |\n| `version` | string | yes | Plugin definition version: \"1.0\" |\n\n---\n\n## 2. Data Format Structure\n\n### 4.1 File Structure\n\nGoose session files use a **two-part JSONL structure**:\n\n#### **Line 1: Session Metadata**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"working_dir\": \"/home/coding/projects/my-app\",\n  \"description\": \"Debug memory leak in worker process\",\n  \"message_count\": 4,\n  \"total_tokens\": 1250,\n  \"input_tokens\": 980,\n  \"output_tokens\": 270,\n  \"accumulated_total_tokens\": 75280,\n  \"accumulated_input_tokens\": 72872,\n  \"accumulated_output_tokens\": 2408\n}\n```\n\n**Session Metadata Fields:**\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|-------------|\n| `working_dir` | string | yes | **Primary project path** - absolute path to project directory |\n| `description` | string | no | Human-readable session description |\n| `message_count` | integer | yes | Number of messages in this session |\n| `total_tokens` | integer | yes | Token count for this session |\n| `input_tokens` | integer | yes | Input tokens for this session |\n| `output_tokens` | integer | yes | Output tokens for this session |\n| `accumulated_total_tokens` | integer | yes | Cumulative total tokens across all sessions |\n| `accumulated_input_tokens` | integer | yes | Cumulative input tokens across all sessions |\n| `accumulated_output_tokens` | integer | yes | Cumulative output tokens across all sessions |\n\n#### **Subsequent Lines: Message Events**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"user\",\n  \"created\": 1747178328,\n  \"content\": [...]\n}\n```\n\n**Message Event Fields:**\n\n| Field | Type | Required | Values | Description |\n|-------|------|----------|--------|-------------|\n| `role` | string | yes | `\"user\"` or `\"assistant\"` | Message role |\n| `created` | integer | yes | Unix timestamp | Seconds since epoch |\n| `content` | array | yes | Content blocks | Array of content block objects (see §4.2) |\n\n### 4.2 Content Block Types\n\nThe `content` array contains blocks of different types that AgentScribe expands into canonical events:\n\n#### Type 1: Text Block\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"text\",\n  \"text\": \"I have started a basic mcp template...\"\n}\n```\n\n**Fields:**\n- `type`: \"text\"\n- `text`: String content of the message\n\n→ Becomes message content text in canonical event\n\n#### Type 2: Tool Request Block\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"toolRequest\",\n  \"id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\",\n  \"toolCall\": {\n    \"status\": \"success\",\n    \"value\": {\n      \"name\": \"developer__shell\",\n      \"arguments\": {\n        \"command\": \"ls -la\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Fields:**\n- `type`: \"toolRequest\"\n- `id`: Tool correlation ID (matches with toolResponse)\n- `toolCall.status`: \"success\" or other status\n- `toolCall.value.name`: Tool name (e.g., \"developer__shell\")\n- `toolCall.value.arguments`: Tool parameters object\n\n→ Expands to `tool_call` canonical event\n\n#### Type 3: Tool Response Block\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"toolResponse\",\n  \"id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\",\n  \"toolResult\": {\n    \"status\": \"success\",\n    \"value\": [...]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n**Fields:**\n- `type`: \"toolResponse\"\n- `id`: Tool correlation ID (matches with toolRequest)\n- `toolResult.status`: \"success\" or other status\n- `toolResult.value`: Tool output (can be nested content blocks)\n\n→ Expands to `tool_result` canonical event\n\n---\n\n## 5. Field Constraints and Validation\n\n### 5.1 Timestamp Field\n\n**Field name:** `created`\n\n**Acceptable values:**\n- Format: Integer (Unix timestamp)\n- Unit: Seconds since epoch\n- Example: `1747178328`\n\n**Constraints:**\n- Must be parseable as integer\n- Represents seconds (not milliseconds)\n- No ISO 8601 format support\n\n### 5.2 Role Field\n\n**Field name:** `role`\n\n**Acceptable values:**\n- `\"user\"` - User message\n- `\"assistant\"` - Assistant message\n\n**Constraints:**\n- Required on all message lines\n- Must be lowercase string\n- No other roles supported (no \"system\", \"tool\", etc. in base role field)\n\n### 5.3 Content Field\n\n**Field name:** `content`\n\n**Acceptable values:**\n- Format: JSON array of content block objects\n- Each block must have `type` field\n- Supported types: \"text\", \"toolRequest\", \"toolResponse\"\n\n**Constraints:**\n- Required on all message lines\n- Must be valid JSON array\n- Cannot be null or undefined\n- Array can contain multiple blocks (e.g., text + toolRequest)\n\n### 5.4 Project Field (working_dir)\n\n**Field name:** `working_dir`\n\n**Acceptable values:**\n- Format: Absolute file path string\n- Example: `\"/home/coding/projects/my-app\"`\n\n**Constraints:**\n- Located in line 1 only (session metadata)\n- Must be absolute path (starts with `/`)\n- Should be valid directory path\n- Not present on message lines\n\n---\n\n## 6. Event Expansion Rules\n\nAgentScribe expands goose content blocks into canonical events as follows:\n\n### 7.1 Text Block → Message Content\n\n```json\n{\"type\":\"text\",\"text\":\"Hello world\"}\n```\n\n→ Canonical event:\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"user\",\n  \"content\": \"Hello world\"\n}\n```\n\n### 7.2 Tool Request → tool_call Event\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"toolRequest\",\n  \"id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\",\n  \"toolCall\": {\n    \"status\": \"success\",\n    \"value\": {\n      \"name\": \"developer__shell\",\n      \"arguments\": {\n        \"command\": \"ls -la\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n\n→ Canonical event:\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"tool_call\",\n  \"tool\": \"developer__shell\",\n  \"content\": \"{\\\"command\\\":\\\"ls -la\\\"}\",\n  \"tool_id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\"\n}\n```\n\n### 7.3 Tool Response → tool_result Event\n\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"toolResponse\",\n  \"id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\",\n  \"toolResult\": {\n    \"status\": \"success\",\n    \"value\": [...]\n  }\n}\n```\n\n→ Canonical event:\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"tool_result\",\n  \"tool\": \"developer__shell\",\n  \"content\": \"...\",\n  \"tool_id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\"\n}\n```\n\n### 7.4 Tool Correlation\n\nTool requests and responses are correlated by the `id` field:\n- `toolRequest.id` == `toolResponse.id` → Same tool interaction\n- ID format: `toolu_<random>_<base62>`\n- AgentScribe matches these to create complete tool call + result pairs\n\n---\n\n## 8. Implementation Notes\n\n### 8.1 Current Implementation Status\n\n**What Works:**\n- ✅ JSONL parsing for standard message lines\n- ✅ Field mapping for timestamp, role, content\n- ✅ Static field assignment (source_agent)\n- ✅ Project detection with `ParentDir` method (fallback)\n\n**Implementation Gaps:**\n- ⚠️ **Field-based project detection for JSONL**: `ProjectDetection::Field` is not fully implemented for JSONL format (parser returns `None` for field-based detection)\n- ⚠️ **First-line metadata extraction**: JSONL parser needs to extract `working_dir` from line 1 and store in ParseContext\n- ⚠️ **content[] array expansion**: Parser needs to expand content blocks into separate canonical events\n\n### 8.2 Current Workaround\n\nIf field-based project detection is not fully implemented, use `ParentDir` method:\n\n```toml\n[parser.project]\nmethod = \"parent_dir\"  # Uses parent directory of session file\n```\n\nThis is less accurate than using `working_dir` from metadata but works immediately.\n\n### 8.3 Differences from Other Agents\n\n| Aspect | Goose | Claude Code | Codex |\n|--------|-------|-------------|-------|\n| **Session metadata location** | Line 1 of JSONL | Separate `session-meta/<uuid>.json` file | Line 1 of JSONL |\n| **Project field** | `working_dir` | `cwd` | `cwd` |\n| **Timestamp format** | Unix timestamp (`created`) | ISO 8601 (`timestamp`) | ISO 8601 (`timestamp`) |\n| **Content structure** | `content[]` array with blocks | Embedded in message with `type` field | Nested `content[]` blocks |\n| **Tool calls** | `toolRequest`/`toolResponse` blocks | `tool_use` content blocks | `function_call`/`function_call_output` |\n| **Model tracking** | Not available | In metadata file | In metadata |\n| **Envelope unwrapping** | Not needed | Not needed | Required |\n\n---\n\n## 9. Goose Plugin Schema\n8\t\n9\t### 1.1 Data Location\n10\t\n11\t- **Path**: `~/.local/share/goose/sessions/*.jsonl`\n12\t- **Format**: JSONL (one JSON object per line)\n13\t\n14\t### 1.2 File Structure\n15\t\n16\tGoose session files have a specific two-part structure:\n17\t\n18\t#### **Line 1: Session Metadata**\n19\t\n20\t```json\n21\t{\n22\t  \"working_dir\": \"/home/coding/projects/my-app\",\n23\t  \"description\": \"Debug memory leak in worker process\",\n24\t  \"message_count\": 4,\n25\t  \"total_tokens\": 1250,\n26\t  \"input_tokens\": 980,\n27\t  \"output_tokens\": 270,\n28\t  \"accumulated_total_tokens\": 75280,\n29\t  \"accumulated_input_tokens\": 72872,\n30\t  \"accumulated_output_tokens\": 2408\n31\t}\n32\t```\n33\t\n34\t**Key fields:**\n35\t- `working_dir`: **Primary project path field** - absolute path to the project directory\n36\t- `description`: Human-readable session description\n37\t- `message_count`: Number of messages in the session\n38\t- `total_tokens`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`: Token counts for this session\n39\t- `accumulated_*`: Cumulative token counts across sessions\n40\t\n41\t#### **Subsequent Lines: Messages**\n42\t\n43\t```json\n44\t{\n45\t  \"role\": \"user\",\n46\t  \"created\": 1747178328,\n47\t  \"content\": [\n48\t    {\n49\t      \"type\": \"text\",\n50\t      \"text\": \"I'm seeing a memory leak in my worker process. Can you help me investigate?\"\n51\t    }\n52\t  ]\n53\t}\n54\t```\n55\t\n56\t**Message fields:**\n57\t- `role`: \"user\" or \"assistant\"\n58\t- `created`: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)\n59\t- `content`: Array of content blocks (text, toolRequest, toolResponse)\n60\t\n61\t### 1.3 Content Block Types\n62\t\n63\tThe `content` array contains blocks of different types that AgentScribe expands into canonical events:\n64\t\n65\t#### Text Block\n66\t```json\n67\t{\n68\t  \"type\": \"text\",\n69\t  \"text\": \"I have started a basic mcp template...\"\n70\t}\n71\t```\n72\t→ Becomes message content text\n73\t\n74\t#### Tool Request Block\n75\t```json\n76\t{\n77\t  \"type\": \"toolRequest\",\n78\t  \"id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\",\n79\t  \"toolCall\": {\n80\t    \"status\": \"success\",\n81\t    \"value\": {\n82\t      \"name\": \"developer__shell\",\n83\t      \"arguments\": {\n84\t        \"command\": \"ls -la\"\n85\t      }\n86\t    }\n87\t  }\n88\t}\n89\t```\n90\t→ Expands to `tool_call` event (extracts tool name from `toolCall.value.name`)\n91\t\n92\t#### Tool Response Block\n93\t```json\n94\t{\n95\t  \"type\": \"toolResponse\",\n96\t  \"id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\",\n97\t  \"toolResult\": {\n98\t    \"status\": \"success\",\n99\t    \"value\": [...]\n100\t  }\n101\t}\n102\t```\n103\t→ Expands to `tool_result` event (correlated with tool_call by `id`)\n104\t\n105\t### 1.4 Required Fields for Plugin Configuration\n106\t\n107\tFor goose, the essential field mappings are:\n108\t\n109\t| Canonical Field | Source Field | Notes |\n110\t|----------------|--------------|-------|\n111\t| `timestamp` | `created` | Unix timestamp (seconds) |\n112\t| `role` | `role` | \"user\" or \"assistant\" |\n113\t| `content` | `content` | Array of content blocks |\n114\t| `project` | `working_dir` | From first-line metadata (line 1) |\n115\t\n116\t## 2. Project Detection Mechanisms\n117\t\n118\t### 2.1 ProjectDetection Enum\n119\t\n120\tAgentScribe supports three project detection strategies defined in `src/plugin.rs`:\n121\t\n122\t```rust\n123\tpub enum ProjectDetection {\n124\t    Field { field: String },  // Extract from a JSON field\n125\t    ParentDir,                // Use parent directory of log file\n126\t    GitRoot,                  // Use git repository root\n127\t}\n128\t```\n129\t\n130\t### 2.2 How ProjectDetection::Field Works\n131\t\n132\t#### Configuration (in `plugins/goose.toml`)\n133\t\n134\t```toml\n135\t[parser.project]\n136\tmethod = \"field\"\n137\tfield = \"working_dir\"\n138\t```\n139\t\n140\t#### Implementation (from `src/scraper/mod.rs`)\n141\t\n142\tThe scraper's `detect_project()` method handles field-based detection:\n143\t\n144\t```rust\n145\t// Line 663-667 in src/scraper/mod.rs\n146\tProjectDetection::Field { field: _ } => {\n147\t    // For field-based detection, we need to extract from the first event\n148\t    // This is handled in the parser, return None here\n149\t    Ok(None)\n150\t}\n151\t```\n152\t\n153\tThis means field-based project detection is **parser-specific**, not scraper-level.\n154\t\n155\t#### Parser Implementation\n156\t\n157\tDifferent parsers handle field-based project detection differently:\n158\t\n159\t**For JSON Array format** (`src/parser/json_array.rs` lines 175-181):\n160\t\n161\t```rust\n162\t// Set project: prefer field extraction from event, fall back to context\n163\tevent.project =\n164\t    if let Some(ProjectDetection::Field { field }) = plugin.parser.project.as_ref() {\n165\t        extract_string(item, field).or_else(|| context.project.clone())\n166\t    } else {\n167\t        context.project.clone()\n168\t    };\n169\t```\n170\t\n171\tThis extracts the project from **each event item**.\n172\t\n173\t**For JSONL format** (`src/parser/jsonl.rs` line 387):\n174\t\n175\t```rust\n176\t// Set project from context\n177\tevent.project = context.project.clone();\n178\t```\n179\t\n180\tJSONL uses the **ParseContext** to carry project information across all events.\n181\t\n182\t### 2.3 How First-Line Metadata Sets Project\n183\t\n184\tThe key insight is that the first line of goose JSONL files contains the session metadata with the `working_dir` field. Here's how it flows:\n185\t\n186\t1. **Parser reads line 1**: Session metadata with `working_dir`\n187\t2. **Extract project field**: Parser should extract `working_dir` from line 1\n188\t3. **Store in ParseContext**: Project value is stored in `ParseContext.project`\n189\t4. **Apply to all events**: Every subsequent event gets `event.project = context.project.clone()`\n190\t\n191\t#### Current Implementation Gap\n192\t\n193\tLooking at the existing code, there's a **missing implementation** for extracting project from first-line metadata in JSONL format:\n194\t\n195\t- The scraper calls `detect_project()` which returns `Ok(None)` for Field detection\n196\t- The ParseContext is created with `project: None` (line 414 in `src/parser/mod.rs`)\n197\t- Events get `event.project = context.project.clone()` which is `None`\n198\t\n199\t**The missing piece**: The JSONL parser needs to:\n200\t1. Read the first line\n201\t2. Extract the project field (e.g., `working_dir`)\n202\t3. Create ParseContext with that project value\n203\t4. Use that context for parsing all subsequent lines\n204\t\n205\t### 2.4 Alternative: ParentDir Detection\n206\t\n207\tIf field-based detection is not implemented, goose can use `ParentDir`:\n208\t\n209\t```toml\n210\t[parser.project]\n211\tmethod = \"parent_dir\"  # Uses parent directory of session file\n212\t```\n213\t\n214\tThis is simpler but less accurate than using the actual `working_dir` from the session metadata.\n215\t\n216\t## 3. Envelope System for First-Line Metadata\n217\t\n218\t### 3.1 What is the Envelope System?\n219\t\n220\tAgentScribe has an **envelope unwrapping system** for handling wrapped JSONL lines where event data is nested inside a wrapper structure (like Codex's `{type, timestamp, payload}` format).\n221\t\n222\t### 3.2 Envelope Configuration\n223\t\n224\t```toml\n225\t[source.envelope]\n226\tpayload_field = \"payload\"    # Field containing actual event data\n227\ttype_field = \"type\"          # Field for routing decisions\n228\ttype_routing = {             # Maps type values to actions\n229\t    message = \"event\",       # → produce canonical events\n230\t    session = \"skip\",        # → ignore this line\n231\t    compaction = \"meta\"      # → accumulate metadata (future)\n232\t}\n233\t```\n234\t\n235\t### 3.3 Routing Actions\n236\t\n237\t- **`\"event\"`**: Extract payload, produce canonical events\n238\t- **`\"skip\"`**: Ignore this line entirely\n239\t- **`\"meta\"`**: Accumulate metadata (not yet fully implemented - returns `Vec::new()`)\n240\t\n241\t### 3.4 Does Goose Need Envelope Unwrapping?\n242\t\n243\t**Current goose plugin**: No envelope configured\n244\t\n245\t**Schema analysis**: Looking at the goose format:\n246\t- Line 1: `{working_dir, description, ...}` - no `type` field, no wrapper\n247\t- Message lines: `{role, created, content[]}` - no wrapper\n248\t\n249\t**Conclusion**: Goose does **NOT** need envelope unwrapping. It's a flat JSONL structure.\n250\t\n251\tThe first line is just a different JSON schema than subsequent lines, not a wrapped structure.\n252\t\n253\t### 3.5 How First-Line Metadata Should Work for Goose\n254\t\n255\tSince goose doesn't use envelope unwrapping, the project extraction should work as follows:\n256\t\n257\t1. **JSONL parser reads first line**: Parse as JSON\n258\t2. **Extract `working_dir` field**: Use the `ProjectDetection::Field { field: \"working_dir\" }` config\n259\t3. **Create ParseContext with project**: \n260\t   ```rust\n261\t   let project = extract_string(&first_line_json, \"working_dir\");\n262\t   let context = ParseContext::new(session_id, source_agent, source_file)\n263\t       .with_project(project);\n264\t   ```\n265\t4. **Parse rest of file with context**: All events get the project from context\n266\t\n267\t## 4. Required Plugin Configuration Fields\n268\t\n269\t### 4.1 Essential Fields for Goose Plugin\n270\t\n271\t```toml\n272\t[plugin]\n273\tname = \"goose\"\n274\tversion = \"1.0\"\n275\t\n276\t[source]\n277\tpaths = [\"~/.local/share/goose/sessions/*.jsonl\"]\n278\tformat = \"jsonl\"\n279\t\n280\t[source.session_detection]\n281\tmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\n282\tsession_id_from = \"filename\"\n283\t\n284\t[parser]\n285\ttimestamp = \"created\"        # Unix timestamp\n286\trole = \"role\"               # \"user\" or \"assistant\"\n287\tcontent = \"content\"         # Array of content blocks\n288\t\n289\t[parser.static]\n290\tsource_agent = \"goose\"\n291\t\n292\t[parser.project]\n293\tmethod = \"field\"            # Extract from first-line metadata\n294\tfield = \"working_dir\"       # Field name in line 1\n295\t\n296\t[parser.model]\n297\tsource = \"none\"             # Model not available in goose logs\n298\t\n299\t[parser.file_paths]\n300\tcontent_regex = true        # Extract paths from content\n301\t```\n302\t\n303\t### 4.2 Field Value Acceptance\n304\t\n305\t#### timestamp field\n306\t- **Accepts**: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)\n307\t- **Format**: Integer or string representing seconds\n308\t- **Example**: `1747178328`\n309\t\n310\t#### role field\n311\t- **Accepts**: \"user\" or \"assistant\"\n312\t- **Format**: String\n313\t- **Required**: Yes - every message line must have a role\n314\t\n315\t#### content field\n316\t- **Accepts**: Array of content blocks\n317\t- **Format**: JSON array with objects containing `type` field\n318\t- **Block types**: \"text\", \"toolRequest\", \"toolResponse\"\n319\t\n320\t#### project field (working_dir)\n321\t- **Accepts**: Absolute file path\n322\t- **Format**: String path\n323\t- **Example**: \"/home/coding/projects/my-app\"\n324\t- **Location**: Line 1 only (session metadata)\n325\t\n326\t## 5. Comparison with Other Plugins\n327\t\n328\t### 5.1 vs Claude Code\n329\t\n330\t| Aspect | Goose | Claude Code |\n331\t|--------|-------|-------------|\n332\t| **Session metadata** | Line 1 of JSONL | Separate `session-meta/<uuid>.json` file |\n333\t| **Project field** | `working_dir` | `cwd` |\n334\t| **Timestamp format** | Unix timestamp (`created`) | ISO 8601 (`timestamp`) |\n335\t| **Content structure** | `content[]` array with blocks | Embedded in message with `type` field |\n336\t| **Tool calls** | `toolRequest`/`toolResponse` blocks | `tool_use` content blocks |\n337\t| **Model tracking** | Not available | In metadata file |\n338\t\n339\t### 5.2 vs Codex\n340\t\n341\t| Aspect | Goose | Codex |\n342\t|--------|-------|-------|\n343\t| **Structure** | Flat JSONL | Envelope-wrapped JSONL |\n344\t| **First line** | Session metadata | `RolloutLine::Meta` |\n345\t| **Type routing** | Not needed | Required (skip/meta/event) |\n346\t| **Project field** | `working_dir` (line 1) | `cwd` (in meta) |\n347\t\n348\t## 6. Goose Plugin Schema\n\n### 1.1 Data Location\n\n- **Path**: `~/.local/share/goose/sessions/*.jsonl`\n- **Format**: JSONL (one JSON object per line)\n\n### 1.2 File Structure\n\nGoose session files have a specific two-part structure:\n\n#### **Line 1: Session Metadata**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"working_dir\": \"/home/coding/projects/my-app\",\n  \"description\": \"Debug memory leak in worker process\",\n  \"message_count\": 4,\n  \"total_tokens\": 1250,\n  \"input_tokens\": 980,\n  \"output_tokens\": 270,\n  \"accumulated_total_tokens\": 75280,\n  \"accumulated_input_tokens\": 72872,\n  \"accumulated_output_tokens\": 2408\n}\n```\n\n**Key fields:**\n- `working_dir`: **Primary project path field** - absolute path to the project directory\n- `description`: Human-readable session description\n- `message_count`: Number of messages in the session\n- `total_tokens`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`: Token counts for this session\n- `accumulated_*`: Cumulative token counts across sessions\n\n#### **Subsequent Lines: Messages**\n\n```json\n{\n  \"role\": \"user\",\n  \"created\": 1747178328,\n  \"content\": [\n    {\n      \"type\": \"text\",\n      \"text\": \"I'm seeing a memory leak in my worker process. Can you help me investigate?\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n```\n\n**Message fields:**\n- `role`: \"user\" or \"assistant\"\n- `created`: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)\n- `content`: Array of content blocks (text, toolRequest, toolResponse)\n\n### 1.3 Content Block Types\n\nThe `content` array contains blocks of different types that AgentScribe expands into canonical events:\n\n#### Text Block\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"text\",\n  \"text\": \"I have started a basic mcp template...\"\n}\n```\n→ Becomes message content text\n\n#### Tool Request Block\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"toolRequest\",\n  \"id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\",\n  \"toolCall\": {\n    \"status\": \"success\",\n    \"value\": {\n      \"name\": \"developer__shell\",\n      \"arguments\": {\n        \"command\": \"ls -la\"\n      }\n    }\n  }\n}\n```\n→ Expands to `tool_call` event (extracts tool name from `toolCall.value.name`)\n\n#### Tool Response Block\n```json\n{\n  \"type\": \"toolResponse\",\n  \"id\": \"toolu_bdrk_01H6Vzjip2dzWDWJMQkiwevZ\",\n  \"toolResult\": {\n    \"status\": \"success\",\n    \"value\": [...]\n  }\n}\n```\n→ Expands to `tool_result` event (correlated with tool_call by `id`)\n\n### 1.4 Required Fields for Plugin Configuration\n\nFor goose, the essential field mappings are:\n\n| Canonical Field | Source Field | Notes |\n|----------------|--------------|-------|\n| `timestamp` | `created` | Unix timestamp (seconds) |\n| `role` | `role` | \"user\" or \"assistant\" |\n| `content` | `content` | Array of content blocks |\n| `project` | `working_dir` | From first-line metadata (line 1) |\n\n## 2. Project Detection Mechanisms\n\n### 2.1 ProjectDetection Enum\n\nAgentScribe supports three project detection strategies defined in `src/plugin.rs`:\n\n```rust\npub enum ProjectDetection {\n    Field { field: String },  // Extract from a JSON field\n    ParentDir,                // Use parent directory of log file\n    GitRoot,                  // Use git repository root\n}\n```\n\n### 2.2 How ProjectDetection::Field Works\n\n#### Configuration (in `plugins/goose.toml`)\n\n```toml\n[parser.project]\nmethod = \"field\"\nfield = \"working_dir\"\n```\n\n#### Implementation (from `src/scraper/mod.rs`)\n\nThe scraper's `detect_project()` method handles field-based detection:\n\n```rust\n// Line 663-667 in src/scraper/mod.rs\nProjectDetection::Field { field: _ } => {\n    // For field-based detection, we need to extract from the first event\n    // This is handled in the parser, return None here\n    Ok(None)\n}\n```\n\nThis means field-based project detection is **parser-specific**, not scraper-level.\n\n#### Parser Implementation\n\nDifferent parsers handle field-based project detection differently:\n\n**For JSON Array format** (`src/parser/json_array.rs` lines 175-181):\n\n```rust\n// Set project: prefer field extraction from event, fall back to context\nevent.project =\n    if let Some(ProjectDetection::Field { field }) = plugin.parser.project.as_ref() {\n        extract_string(item, field).or_else(|| context.project.clone())\n    } else {\n        context.project.clone()\n    };\n```\n\nThis extracts the project from **each event item**.\n\n**For JSONL format** (`src/parser/jsonl.rs` line 387):\n\n```rust\n// Set project from context\nevent.project = context.project.clone();\n```\n\nJSONL uses the **ParseContext** to carry project information across all events.\n\n### 2.3 How First-Line Metadata Sets Project\n\nThe key insight is that the first line of goose JSONL files contains the session metadata with the `working_dir` field. Here's how it flows:\n\n1. **Parser reads line 1**: Session metadata with `working_dir`\n2. **Extract project field**: Parser should extract `working_dir` from line 1\n3. **Store in ParseContext**: Project value is stored in `ParseContext.project`\n4. **Apply to all events**: Every subsequent event gets `event.project = context.project.clone()`\n\n#### Current Implementation Gap\n\nLooking at the existing code, there's a **missing implementation** for extracting project from first-line metadata in JSONL format:\n\n- The scraper calls `detect_project()` which returns `Ok(None)` for Field detection\n- The ParseContext is created with `project: None` (line 414 in `src/parser/mod.rs`)\n- Events get `event.project = context.project.clone()` which is `None`\n\n**The missing piece**: The JSONL parser needs to:\n1. Read the first line\n2. Extract the project field (e.g., `working_dir`)\n3. Create ParseContext with that project value\n4. Use that context for parsing all subsequent lines\n\n### 2.4 Alternative: ParentDir Detection\n\nIf field-based detection is not implemented, goose can use `ParentDir`:\n\n```toml\n[parser.project]\nmethod = \"parent_dir\"  # Uses parent directory of session file\n```\n\nThis is simpler but less accurate than using the actual `working_dir` from the session metadata.\n\n## 3. Envelope System for First-Line Metadata\n\n### 3.1 What is the Envelope System?\n\nAgentScribe has an **envelope unwrapping system** for handling wrapped JSONL lines where event data is nested inside a wrapper structure (like Codex's `{type, timestamp, payload}` format).\n\n### 3.2 Envelope Configuration\n\n```toml\n[source.envelope]\npayload_field = \"payload\"    # Field containing actual event data\ntype_field = \"type\"          # Field for routing decisions\ntype_routing = {             # Maps type values to actions\n    message = \"event\",       # → produce canonical events\n    session = \"skip\",        # → ignore this line\n    compaction = \"meta\"      # → accumulate metadata (future)\n}\n```\n\n### 3.3 Routing Actions\n\n- **`\"event\"`**: Extract payload, produce canonical events\n- **`\"skip\"`**: Ignore this line entirely\n- **`\"meta\"`**: Accumulate metadata (not yet fully implemented - returns `Vec::new()`)\n\n### 3.4 Does Goose Need Envelope Unwrapping?\n\n**Current goose plugin**: No envelope configured\n\n**Schema analysis**: Looking at the goose format:\n- Line 1: `{working_dir, description, ...}` - no `type` field, no wrapper\n- Message lines: `{role, created, content[]}` - no wrapper\n\n**Conclusion**: Goose does **NOT** need envelope unwrapping. It's a flat JSONL structure.\n\nThe first line is just a different JSON schema than subsequent lines, not a wrapped structure.\n\n### 3.5 How First-Line Metadata Should Work for Goose\n\nSince goose doesn't use envelope unwrapping, the project extraction should work as follows:\n\n1. **JSONL parser reads first line**: Parse as JSON\n2. **Extract `working_dir` field**: Use the `ProjectDetection::Field { field: \"working_dir\" }` config\n3. **Create ParseContext with project**: \n   ```rust\n   let project = extract_string(&first_line_json, \"working_dir\");\n   let context = ParseContext::new(session_id, source_agent, source_file)\n       .with_project(project);\n   ```\n4. **Parse rest of file with context**: All events get the project from context\n\n## 4. Required Plugin Configuration Fields\n\n### 4.1 Essential Fields for Goose Plugin\n\n```toml\n[plugin]\nname = \"goose\"\nversion = \"1.0\"\n\n[source]\npaths = [\"~/.local/share/goose/sessions/*.jsonl\"]\nformat = \"jsonl\"\n\n[source.session_detection]\nmethod = \"one-file-per-session\"\nsession_id_from = \"filename\"\n\n[parser]\ntimestamp = \"created\"        # Unix timestamp\nrole = \"role\"               # \"user\" or \"assistant\"\ncontent = \"content\"         # Array of content blocks\n\n[parser.static]\nsource_agent = \"goose\"\n\n[parser.project]\nmethod = \"field\"            # Extract from first-line metadata\nfield = \"working_dir\"       # Field name in line 1\n\n[parser.model]\nsource = \"none\"             # Model not available in goose logs\n\n[parser.file_paths]\ncontent_regex = true        # Extract paths from content\n```\n\n### 4.2 Field Value Acceptance\n\n#### timestamp field\n- **Accepts**: Unix timestamp (seconds since epoch)\n- **Format**: Integer or string representing seconds\n- **Example**: `1747178328`\n\n#### role field\n- **Accepts**: \"user\" or \"assistant\"\n- **Format**: String\n- **Required**: Yes - every message line must have a role\n\n#### content field\n- **Accepts**: Array of content blocks\n- **Format**: JSON array with objects containing `type` field\n- **Block types**: \"text\", \"toolRequest\", \"toolResponse\"\n\n#### project field (working_dir)\n- **Accepts**: Absolute file path\n- **Format**: String path\n- **Example**: \"/home/coding/projects/my-app\"\n- **Location**: Line 1 only (session metadata)\n\n## 5. Comparison with Other Plugins\n\n### 5.1 vs Claude Code\n\n| Aspect | Goose | Claude Code |\n|--------|-------|-------------|\n| **Session metadata** | Line 1 of JSONL | Separate `session-meta/<uuid>.json` file |\n| **Project field** | `working_dir` | `cwd` |\n| **Timestamp format** | Unix timestamp (`created`) | ISO 8601 (`timestamp`) |\n| **Content structure** | `content[]` array with blocks | Embedded in message with `type` field |\n| **Tool calls** | `toolRequest`/`toolResponse` blocks | `tool_use` content blocks |\n| **Model tracking** | Not available | In metadata file |\n\n### 5.2 vs Codex\n\n| Aspect | Goose | Codex |\n|--------|-------|-------|\n| **Structure** | Flat JSONL | Envelope-wrapped JSONL |\n| **First line** | Session metadata | `RolloutLine::Meta` |\n| **Type routing** | Not needed | Required (skip/meta/event) |\n| **Project field** | `working_dir` (line 1) | `cwd` (in meta) |\n\n## 6. Current Implementation Status\n\n### 6.1 What Works\n\n- ✅ JSONL parsing for standard message lines\n- ✅ Field mapping for timestamp, role, content\n- ✅ Static field assignment (source_agent)\n- ✅ Project detection with ParentDir method\n\n### 6.2 What Needs Implementation\n\n- ⚠️ **First-line metadata extraction**: JSONL parser needs to read line 1, extract project field, and store in ParseContext\n- ⚠️ **Field-based project detection for JSONL**: Currently only implemented for JsonArray format, not Jsonl\n- ⚠️ **content[] array expansion**: Parser needs to expand content blocks into separate events (text → content, toolRequest → tool_call, toolResponse → tool_result)\n\n### 6.3 Current Workaround\n\nThe current goose plugin configuration uses:\n\n```toml\n[parser.project]\nmethod = \"field\"\nfield = \"working_dir\"\n```\n\nBut this relies on parser-level extraction that may not be fully implemented. Summary and Recommendations\n\n### 7.1 Schema Requirements\n\nThe goose plugin requires:\n1. **Line 1 handling**: Extract session metadata (`working_dir`, `description`, etc.)\n2. **Field-based project detection**: Implement `ProjectDetection::Field` for JSONL format\n3. **Content array expansion**: Parse `content[]` blocks into canonical events\n4. **Tool correlation**: Match `toolRequest.id` with `toolResponse.id`\n\n### 7.2 Project Detection Field Values\n\nFor goose, the project detection field is:\n- **Field name**: `working_dir`\n- **Location**: Line 1 (first line of JSONL file)\n- **Format**: Absolute file path string\n- **Example value**: `/home/coding/projects/my-app`\n\n### 7.3 Ready to Create Config\n\nWith this understanding, you can create a functional goose plugin configuration using:\n\n1. **Project detection**: `method = \"field\"` with `field = \"working_dir\"` (requires parser implementation) OR `method = \"parent_dir\"` (works immediately)\n2. **Timestamp field**: `timestamp = \"created\"` (Unix timestamp)\n3. **Role field**: `role = \"role\"` (user/assistant)\n4. **Content field**: `content = \"content\"` (array of blocks)\n\n### 7.4 Next Steps\n\nTo fully support goose with accurate project detection:\n\n1.
